subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which 14-year-old's brutal 1955 murder in Mississippi became a catalyst for the civil rights movement?
questions.explain: The murder of Emmett Till in 1955, and his mother's open-casket funeral, galvanised the movement.

questions.q: At which 1963 event did Martin Luther King deliver his 'I Have a Dream' speech?
questions.explain: King gave the speech to over 200,000 people at the March on Washington in 1963.

questions.q: In which year was Martin Luther King assassinated in Memphis, Tennessee?
questions.explain: Martin Luther King was shot dead on 4 April 1968.

questions.q: At the 1968 Mexico City Olympics, two African American athletes raised gloved fists in which gesture?
options: The clenched fist of unity only
questions.explain: Tommie Smith and John Carlos gave the Black Power salute at the 1968 Olympics.

questions.q: Whose refusal to give up her bus seat in 1955 sparked the Montgomery Bus Boycott?
questions.explain: Rosa Parks's arrest in Montgomery, Alabama triggered the year-long boycott.

questions.q: In 1957 federal troops were sent to enable nine black students to attend a high school in which city?
questions.explain: The Little Rock Nine integrated Central High School in Arkansas in 1957.

questions.q: Which leader became prominent in the Nation of Islam and rejected non-violence before his 1965 assassination?
questions.explain: Malcolm X advocated black self-defence and was assassinated in 1965.

questions.q: The 1954 Supreme Court ruling that segregated schools were unconstitutional was known as which case?
questions.explain: Brown v Board of Education (1954) declared school segregation unconstitutional.

questions.q: In 1963 police used dogs and fire hoses against child protesters in which Alabama city?
questions.explain: The 1963 Birmingham campaign saw police use dogs and fire hoses on young marchers.

questions.q: What system of state and local laws enforced racial segregation in the southern USA?
questions.explain: Jim Crow laws enforced segregation in the South until the 1960s.

questions.q: Which leader popularised the 'Black Power' slogan within SNCC from 1966?
questions.explain: Stokely Carmichael popularised the 'Black Power' slogan in 1966.

questions.q: Which civil rights organisation did Martin Luther King help found and lead from 1957?
questions.explain: King helped found the Southern Christian Leadership Conference in 1957.

questions.q: Which militant group, founded in 1966, used the slogan 'Black Power' and patrolled with weapons?
questions.explain: The Black Panther Party was founded in 1966 by Huey Newton and Bobby Seale.

questions.q: Which interracial bus journeys in 1961 challenged segregation on interstate travel in the South?
questions.explain: The 1961 Freedom Rides tested the desegregation of interstate buses and terminals.

questions.q: The 1960 protests where black students refused to leave whites-only lunch counters began in which city?
questions.explain: The lunch-counter sit-in movement began in Greensboro, North Carolina in 1960.

questions.q: Which NAACP field worker was assassinated in Mississippi in 1963?
questions.explain: Civil rights activist Medgar Evers was murdered in Mississippi in 1963.

questions.q: Which organisation, founded in 1909, used the courts to challenge segregation, including the Brown case?
questions.explain: The NAACP led the legal campaign that produced the 1954 Brown v Board victory.

questions.q: The 1965 Voting Rights Act followed marches centred on which Alabama city?
questions.explain: The Selma marches highlighted black voter suppression and led to the 1965 Act.

questions.q: In 1962 federal marshals were sent to enrol James Meredith as the first black student at which university?
questions.explain: James Meredith integrated the University of Mississippi ('Ole Miss') in 1962 amid violent resistance.

questions.q: Which Act, passed after Selma, banned literacy tests and protected black voter registration?
questions.explain: The 1965 Voting Rights Act outlawed discriminatory voting barriers like literacy tests.

questions.q: What earlier 1896 Supreme Court ruling established the 'separate but equal' doctrine later overturned?
questions.explain: Plessy v Ferguson (1896) upheld 'separate but equal' segregation.

questions.q: Which student-led civil rights group, founded in 1960, organised sit-ins and Freedom Rides?
questions.explain: The Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC) was founded in 1960.
